title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Brent crude back above $90/bbl after the US and Iran traded strikes near the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, with missiles also fired at Jordan
Markets: 10-year Treasury yields near their highest since January 2025; September Fed rate-hike odds jumped to ~66%, up from ~41% a week ago
Markets: Major indexes closed lower Monday (S&P 500 -0.3%, Nasdaq -0.1%, Dow -374 pts/-0.7%), though August still ended strong (S&P +2.5%, Nasdaq +3%, Dow +1.3% for the month)
Companies: FTC sues Amazon, alleging it manipulated its ad auction system to overcharge advertisers by tens of billions of dollars; shares fell 2.5%
Companies: PG&E (-20%) and Edison International (-23%) tumbled after California lawmakers rejected a Newsom-backed shield against utility wildfire lawsuits
Companies: Palo Alto Networks and Dell report quarterly earnings after today's close; Medtronic reports before the bell
Macro/Policy: US-Iran hostilities resumed after a roughly month-long pause, adding inflation and rate-path uncertainty ahead of the Sept. 15-16 FOMC meeting
Macro/Policy: August ISM manufacturing data and July construction spending figures are due Tuesday
